(3) F-DG6-362 (Medium): the instrumented sweep shows that 31 of its 383 operation ids answer 400 to every reader it checks, because their required query parameters are not filled. Among them are getExecutiveOverview, getFinanceDashboard, getAdoptionDashboard, getDashboardDrilldown, listAuditEvents and listBusinessCases. It also reads lists on their first 25 items only (log 46). No other leak: part A, 230 paginated list reads followed to the last page, 0 leaks. Part B: the finance and adoption dashboards and every other drill-down metric and class, 0 leaks. listAuditEvents for AUD over all 7 pages and filtered to the benefit, its case and the ask, 0 leaks; TL gets 403 there. listTransformationAudit over all 7 pages for TL and AUD, 0 leaks; the admitted TL does see the title, the positive control. Part C: after the real reindex, the benefit's document is indexed but never returned to TL or AUD. The ask's document is titled 'CA-01' (the case code, BE-Z5's neutral title) and is returned to them, which is acceptable (it names no benefit code, title or value). Part D: the live registers(benefits) export as TL gives 403 export.includes_restricted_records, and so does the admitted TL's benefits snapshot. The other registers are accepted (202): they hold no benefit row, and their sources are re-checked by the assembly watch. Part E: no inbox notification holds the title. 400-ops probe: listBusinessCases, listInitiatives, listDecisions, listSensitiveGrants and the rest answer 200 with transformationId and leak nothing; only the overview leaks. Residuals: (i) the 71 unfillable operations are listed accurately (the same 71 in log 46) and are not benefit-derived, apart from three that are guarded per path parameter. Acceptable as a list, but the sweep's coverage claim is overstated (F-DG6-362). (ii) Search, not exercised by the sweep: exercised here with the real indexer, no leak, acceptable. (iii) Stored rows from before the fix keep a benefit title: acceptable, because no released environment exists (DG7 is not passed), the affected rows are a benefit child (the corrective case, hidden) or an ask created before the fix, and new asks are titled by the case code. It should be recorded as a pre-release data note. (iv) Benefit ids and codes in the frozen G6 snapshot (g6SnapshotOf also carries `code`, which the handback does not mention): acceptable. They are ids and codes without title or values, accepted for frozen G6 and closure snapshots in round 3, and consistent with the case-code residual. (v) The counts kept as truthful verdicts (the G6 placeholder, hiddenItemCount, the frozen itemCount, report totals, benefit_missing): acceptable under ADR-0051 §8 and D-195 Q3, since aggregates are the same for every reader and show no individual value. Other paths read: the meeting output create checks only that the record exists, not that the caller may read it. So a TL can learn that a uuid is a benefit of the transformation (201 versus 422), but sees no title or value. Ids are already disclosed in the G6 snapshot, so this is not raised. Handover acceptance sets bau_owner on a linked sensitive benefit for a receiving owner who is not admitted; that is a write by design of the handover, which an admitted user linked, and it discloses ids only. Report assemblers emit no benefit-child source type that the export check (SENSITIVE_SOURCE_TYPES) lacks.

checks_run.procedure: Review rebaseOverSystemOccurrences (operations/exceptions.ts) against the 0101 guard and history trigger. Judge whether the re-raise rule hides a real conflict, loses a system update, or lets a stale human write overwrite a newer human one. Run its tests and the a22 e2e.
checks_run.command: git diff 654e39d..d7b21bad -- apps/api/src/modules/operations/exceptions.ts; packages/db/migrations/0101 (operational_exception_guard, operational_exception_history); exception-recurrence-race.test.ts in CS-07/CS-08; e2e/a22-p6-operability.spec.ts in CS-15
checks_run.environment: source at d7b21bad; the suites as cited
checks_run.expected: no hidden conflict, no lost update, no stale overwrite
checks_run.actual: Sound. The rule accepts an If-Match behind the locked row only when every version after it is a history event of kind 'recurred' with actor NULL, and when there is exactly one event per version (after.length = locked.version - expected). Anything else gives the shared 409: an acknowledgement, a resolution, a 'recovered' auto-resolution, an 'updated' event, a version ahead of the row, or a non-integer or a value below 1. Why it cannot hide a conflict: the 0101 history trigger labels an update 'recurred' only when occurrence_count changes and the status does not move to acknowledged or resolved. The guard forbids a reopen (acknowledged to open, resolved to anything) and records an acknowledgement once. So a recurrence never changes what a human acts on: the status, the acknowledgement or the resolution. Nothing is lost, because the human update is applied to the locked current row, so the system's occurrence_count, last_error and failure link stay. Two humans on the same loaded version still give 409, which is tested. A recurrence raised with a user actor gives 409, which is conservative. The audit event records based_on_version {from, to}. exception-recurrence-race.test.ts (7 tests) passes in both locales (CS-07/CS-08), and a22-p6-operability passes in en and ar (CS-15). The e2e helper ageExceptionOccurrence interpolates the exception id into SQL only after a uuid regex check; it is test-only.
